requestKey: How do I plan outfits from my own wardrobe?|cherly.app|sample2

payload.text:
Great question. Here’s a simple, repeatable way to plan outfits using only what you already own.

Quick start (20 minutes for the coming week)
- Check your calendar and the 7‑day forecast. Note dress codes, special events, and the most extreme temp each day.
- Choose your anchors first: 2 pairs of shoes that work for most plans + 1 everyday bag. This quietly decides colors and formality.
- Pull 8–12 versatile pieces around those anchors: 4–5 tops, 3–4 bottoms, 1–2 layers, 1–2 dresses/jumpsuits.
- Use “outfit equations” to make 5–7 looks. Try on fast, adjust, and take a quick mirror photo of each.
- Hang each outfit together (or in a labeled album on your phone) so mornings are grab‑and‑go.

Outfit equations that almost always work
- Blazer or cardigan + tee/tank + jeans/trousers + loafers/sneakers.
- Dress + light layer (denim jacket, cardigan, blazer) + flats/boots.
- Wide‑leg trousers + fitted knit or tee + belt + low heels/sneakers.
- Midi skirt + simple top + cropped jacket + boots/sandals.
- Monochrome column (top and bottom same color) + contrast jacket + matching shoes/belt.
- Casual: structured sweatshirt/knit + straight jeans + clean sneakers + watch.

Proportion cheat sheet
- Long over lean: oversized/topper + slim bottom.
- Short over volume: cropped/shorter top + wide‑leg or full skirt.
- One volume piece at a time to avoid looking swamped.
- If shoes are chunky, keep pants cropped or tapered; if pants are wide/long, choose a sleeker shoe.

Build a small “cluster” from your closet
- Pick a palette: 2 base neutrals, 1 supporting neutral, 2 accent colors you actually wear.
- Create a 7‑piece cluster: 3 tops, 2 bottoms, 1 layer, 1 dress or wildcard. Aim for every top to match both bottoms.
- Add 2 shoes and 2 accessories. This easily yields 12–20 outfits without buying anything.

Weekly planning flow
1) Calendar + weather: list activities and temperature ranges by day.
2) Choose shoes first for each day, then bottoms, then top, then a “third piece” (jacket, vest, scarf) and 1–2 accessories.
3) Fit/comfort check: can you sit, walk, reach? Swap now, not at 7am.
4) Photograph and name the look (“Black blazer/striped tee/blue jeans/loafers”) so you can repeat later.
5) Prep station: steam, lint‑roll, place socks/undergarments, and set aside the right outerwear.

Make your own lookbook
- Use a phone album with tags like Work, Casual, Dressy, Hot, Cold, Rain.
- Track wears briefly in Notes or a spreadsheet: date, occasion, comfort rating, anything you’d tweak.
- After 4–6 weeks, spotlight your “all‑stars” and note true gaps (e.g., no light neutral belt, need rain‑friendly shoes).

Smart mixing tips
- Patterns: pair one print with solids that match one color in the print; or mix prints by keeping one small‑scale and one large‑scale in the same color family.
- Texture: add depth with one textured piece (linen, leather, knit, denim) per outfit.
- Color: repeat a color at least twice (e.g., stripe color echoed in shoes or bag) to look intentional.

Common pitfalls and easy fixes
- Too many “orphans” that match nothing: create a mini‑cluster around a favorite orphan or let it go.
- Great outfits, impractical shoes: plan from the ground up; comfort first.
- Laundry bottlenecks: duplicate your most‑worn base layers or neutrals.
- Weather whiplash: keep a thin packable layer and small umbrella with your work bag.

If you want, upload a few photos of your favorite pieces (or a quick list by color and category) and tell me:
- Your typical week (work/casual/dressy mix) and climate
- Any items you struggle to style
- Colors you love or avoid
I can turn that into a 10–15‑outfit capsule from your existing wardrobe.
